anti_overlap: Do not do speech-act taxonomy or sentence-force classification — no enumerating utterance types, no assertion-versus-question analysis, no philosophical refinement of what 'assert' means. That is the definition-extension track's territory.

Do not argue definitions by counter-instance and logical over-extension; argue them by what they certify to a downstream consumer and by measured rates. Where a semantic point is unavoidable, state it in one line and move to the measurement.

Do not review model choice, MLX runtime behaviour, batching, quantisation, prompt caching, throughput or cost. Instrument capability is in scope only where it limits what the standard can be defined as.

Do not perform general code review — no style, typing, test-coverage or refactor findings. A finding qualifies only if it changes the standard, the threshold policy, the sampling plane, or what the label warrants.
Do not redesign the JTMS, the tension feed, the ranking function, or the stance-detection edge. The subject is the gate's standard and its mark.
decision_lens: Rank a candidate definition by what it warrants to the consumer of the mark. Ask, for each: what must be true of a post for extract_prompt.py to yield a non-NONE commitment and for pairing.py to be able to collide it — and does this definition certify that, or something weaker that merely correlates with it? Prefer the standard that is (a) fixed by downstream use, (b) testable by the instrument actually in hand, and (c) publishable with a remedy band the office would defend. A definition that is right in principle but only assayable by cupellation must say so and name the reserved-sample protocol that would verify it.
distance_rationale: A pre-modern physical-craft discipline with no contact with language, classification, or software. Its entire professional apparatus exists to answer a question with the same shape as the one under review: what counts as the substance, by what test, at what threshold, and who is answerable for the mark. Crucially the trade settled long ago that the standard is a convention fixed by downstream use rather than a natural kind — silver is 925/1000 because pure silver will not survive circulation — which is precisely the move this review needs and which no purely semantic analysis of 'claim' will produce. It also carries centuries of hard-won knowledge about how a fast surface test is systematically fooled, which a probabilistic gate reading one token has no vocabulary for.
expected_isomorphisms: The sterling standard (a purity threshold chosen for what the metal must later withstand) ≅ the definition of 'claim' chosen for what pairing.py and tension_prompt.py must later do with it; touchstone-and-needles (fast, comparative, surface-only, ideal for triage) ≅ a single-token logit gate, versus cupellation (destructive, quantitative, gives real fineness) ≅ actually running extraction and seeing whether a commitment survives; surface enrichment and blanching (a debased coin boiled to leave a pure skin) ≅ posts with assertoric surface over no propositional content; plating ≅ 'total kittification of the simcluster' at p=0.999; quartation (parting only works after the alloy is diluted into a particular concentration regime) ≅ a separation prompt operating outside the regime where its reagent can discriminate; the remedy (an explicit published tolerance around the standard) ≅ the 722 posts in the 0.4–0.6 band binarised by argmax; the assay office's warrant and its liability for the mark ≅ what downstream stages are entitled to assume when they see label=claim; the Trial of the Pyx (independent annual re-assay of a reserved random sample by an outside jury) ≅ the planned local-versus-Haiku agreement check; assay sampling from prescribed drilling points because alloys segregate ≅ the prefilter deciding which population is presented for assay at all.
focus: Setting the fineness standard from downstream use rather than from the folk sense of the word: which sense of 'claim' the gate can physically test, which sense the design needs, what the label warrants to the stages that consume it, and whether the 34% figure is a definition error, a sampling error, or a standard error.
name: fd-assay-fineness-warrant
persona: Apply the perspective of an assay master — the officer of a guild assay office whose trade is deciding, on physical evidence and against a published standard, whether a piece may carry the mark. Three habits define the practice. First, the standard is chosen for what the metal must later do, never for metaphysical purity: sterling is 925 because coin and plate must survive wear, so the question is always 'fine enough for what'. Second, tests are ranked by what they can be fooled by: the touchstone is fast and comparative and reads only the skin, so it triages, while cupellation destroys the sample and returns a number, and a shop that reports touchstone results as fineness will eventually mark plated brass. Third, the mark is a warrant with liability attached — the office is answerable for every piece it strikes, so it publishes a remedy (an explicit tolerance) rather than pretending to a bright line, reserves samples for independent re-assay, and specifies where in the piece the drilling is taken because alloys segregate and a sample from the wrong plane assays a different metal than the one being sold.
review_areas: Derive the standard from downstream use before judging any candidate: read extract_prompt.py, pairing.py and tension_prompt.py and state what a post must carry for a commitment to be extractable and collidable. Then rank the five senses by how closely each certifies that property rather than by how well each matches the ordinary word 'claim'.

Separate the sense the gate can TEST from the sense the design WANTS. Name the surface properties a one-token judgment can actually reach (declarative form, hedge markers, topical substance, length, joke framing) and identify the plating failures — posts with an assertoric skin over no propositional content that pass at high probability — with quoted examples.

Reconcile 34% against the ~3% estimate by elimination, not assertion: check whether the two figures are over the same population (post-prefilter versus whole corpus), whether the prefilter's removals changed the composition of what was assayed, and whether the two numbers even name the same standard. Report which of the three explanations the data supports and what measurement would settle the remainder.

Treat prob and mass as instrument readings with known failure modes. mass says the model answered; prob is a comparative streak, not a fineness. Test whether prob has any monotone relationship to a cupellation-grade outcome — e.g. whether higher-prob claims yield non-NONE extractions more often — on a small reserved sample, and say plainly what a threshold sweep on prob can and cannot buy.

Design the remedy: the 0.4–0.6 band holds 722 posts currently binarised by argmax, and the repeated p=0.5622 across unrelated texts suggests the model is returning a prior rather than a judgment there. Propose which candidate definition supports an explicit tolerance band (admit / contested / reject) and what the contested tier costs downstream, given the pipeline already surfaces contested findings elsewhere.

State the warrant for each of the five senses: what a downstream stage is entitled to assume when it reads label=claim, and whether extract_prompt.py and pairing.py in fact rely on a stronger warrant than the gate can issue. Where a candidate definition can only be verified destructively, specify the reserved-sample re-assay (size, selection rule, second family) that would make the mark defensible.

severity_examples.condition: P0 only if the mismatch is demonstrated concretely — a class of posts the current standard admits that extraction or pairing provably cannot use, or a class it rejects that would have produced collidable commitments — not inferred from the rubric's wording alone.
severity_examples.scenario: The standard is being set from the ordinary sense of 'claim' rather than from what the tension stage can collide, so the gate is being tuned toward a fineness no consumer of the mark needs. Every subsequent rubric revision, threshold sweep and agreement check would then be optimising the assay against the wrong standard, and the whole run could come back correct and useless.

severity_examples.condition: P1 when the counter-evidence is drawn from real scored lines across bands; P2 if the concern is real but the proposed remedy is only a diagnostic to run rather than a change to the definition or threshold policy.
severity_examples.scenario: prob is being read as fineness when it is a comparative streak: sub-40-character fragments such as 'total kittification of the simcluster' sit at p=0.999 alongside genuine hedged assertions, so a threshold sweep on prob would move volume without moving purity. Any claim-definition ranked on the assumption that a higher cutoff yields a purer set is resting on an untested instrument reading.

severity_examples.condition: P2 when it degrades yield without invalidating a decision; raise to P1 if the band turns out to contain a disproportionate share of the belief-bearing posts the acceptance criterion depends on.
severity_examples.scenario: The 0.4–0.6 band is discarded into binary labels with no remedy policy, and the recurrence of p=0.5622 across unrelated texts indicates those verdicts carry no judgment at all. The label scorer already yields the tolerance information for free and the pipeline already has a 'contested' idiom; not using it throws away the cheapest available quality lever.

source_domain: Assaying and hallmarking — the guild craft of certifying metal fineness (touchstone and needles, cupellation, quartation and parting, the sterling standard and its remedy, the assay office's warrant, the Trial of the Pyx), refined continuously since the thirteenth century
success_hints: Establish the downstream requirement first by reading extract_prompt.py, pairing.py and tension_prompt.py, then work backwards to the standard. A ranking of definitions produced before knowing what the consumer needs is a ranking against no standard at all.

Compute rather than estimate: read data/gate.jsonl and data/posts.jsonl and report actual counts and rates per band, per length bucket, and per structural class (reply, quote-post with little own text, top-level). The 34% is only interpretable once you know what the prefilter left in the crucible.

Check whether the ~3% design figure and the 34% measurement share a denominator before treating the gap as a defect. Two honest numbers over different populations are not a contradiction, and reporting them as one would send the rubric revision the wrong way.

Prefer a small destructive test to a large inferential argument: running extraction over a reserved sample stratified by prob answers what the label warrants far more cheaply than reasoning about it, and the result is reportable either way.

Say what each candidate definition would make the claim rate, and whether that rate is affordable given the extraction and pairing volumes in the brainstorm's cascade table. A standard that cannot be run is not a standard.

Be explicit about which direction of error the standard should favour and why. The brainstorm argues false negatives are the dangerous and unobservable side at this stage; a remedy band is the trade's answer to exactly that asymmetry, and any recommendation should say what it costs.
task_context:
What does 'claim' mean in this pipeline? The gate (src/norvid_studier/gate_prompt.py) sorts 40,943 prefiltered Bluesky posts into claim/nonclaim and has now scored ~33k of them into data/gate.jsonl (each line: uri, label, prob, mass, top_token). Downstream, extract_prompt.py turns each claim into a 'commitment', pairing.py finds candidate contradictory pairs, and tension_prompt.py judges them. The acceptance criterion for the whole system is norvid_studies' words: 'found things I didn't notice but upon juxtaposition oh yeah those cant both be right'. Determine the top 5 candidate DEFINITIONS of 'claim' the gate could be operating on — not five example claims, five rival senses of the word — and rank them by how well each serves that acceptance criterion. Ground every candidate in the ACTUAL scored data: read data/gate.jsonl and data/posts.jsonl, sample real posts at various prob levels, and show which definition each real verdict is consistent with. Known symptoms to explain: questions still score YES despite an explicit NO rule; 'holy heck' scores as a claim; ~34% claim rate is ~10x the design estimate of belief-bearing posts (~3%); the rubric asks for 'asserts something that could be true or false, and that its author could be asked to defend' which conflates at least assertion-vs-question, proposition-vs-speech-act, and defensible-vs-sincere. Read docs/brainstorms/2026-07-29-norvid-studier-brainstorm.md for prior reasoning.

This review contributes the fineness-and-warrant track. The ~3% design estimate and the measured ~34% (12,309 of 34,317 scored lines) may not be figures about the same population or the same standard: the brainstorm's 0.5–1% 'belief-bearing seam' was reasoned over the whole 53,783-post corpus, whereas the gate assays only what the prefilter presented, and a heuristic prefilter that removes bare fragments changes the alloy before the test. Establishing whether the gap is a definition error, a sampling-plane error, or a comparison between two different standards is prior to any rubric change. Also material: LabelScore in gate_prompt.py exposes prob (renormalised across the two label tokens) and mass (total probability on any label token, with min_trustworthy_mass = 0.9); the 200-post bench measured mass ≥ 0.9 on 200/200, which establishes that the model answered the question, not that it assayed correctly. Real verdicts worth explaining: 'holy heck' → claim at p=0.731 while 'holy heck dude' → nonclaim at p=0.953; 1,710 claim-labelled posts under 40 characters, many above p=0.99; 722 posts in the 0.4–0.6 band, several of them at exactly p=0.5622 across wildly different texts.
